reflection we are called to serve one another. at emmaus café, humble service, gentle listening, and care reveal christ, reflecting the disciples’ encounter with him. “serve one another humbly in love.” (galatians 5:13) bishop antony mar silvanos visi ts bishop fintan in cork bishop antony mar silvanos, curia bishop of the syro- malankara catholic church, visited bishop fintan gavin at the cork and ross diocesan centre on 2 october. he was accompanied by fr shinu varghese, national coordinator of the syro-malankara catholic church ireland. the visit provided an opportunity for a cordial meeting and fellowship. remembering bishop michael murphy 30th anniv ersary the cork cathedral family of parishes remembers bishop michael murphy, former bishop of cork and ross, on the 30th anniversary of his death on 7 october 1996. bishop murphy served as bishop of cork and ross from 1980 until his passing in 1996, dedicating many years to the church and the communities of the diocese. one of his lasting contributions was overseeing the major renovation and restoration of the cathedral of st mary and st anne, commonly known as the north cathedral, between 1994 and 1996. the cathedral was rededicated on 29 september 1996, with bishop murphy presiding over what would be his final public function, just eight days before his passing. thirty years on, we remember bishop murphy with gratitude for his years of service, his contribution to the diocese of cork and ross, and his lasting connection to our cathedral. bishop murphy also laid the foundation stone of st oliver’s church in ballyvolane in december 1991. may he rest in peace. office hours in the family of parishes cathedral parish office monday to thursday 8:30am-4pm friday 8:30am-2pm st finbarr’s south removed_lines: community in action at st oliv er’s church singing for the brain brings the community together it was wonderful to see st oliver’s church full of music, movement and conversation recently as members of the local community came together for a singing for the brain session.
facilitated by ceara, the session involved much more than singing, with participants taking part in breathing exercises, movement and activities designed to engage both the body and mind.
most importantly, it provided an opportunity for people to come toge ther, enjoy each other’s company and take part in something positive within their local community.
founded by fiona flavin of the hse, singing for the brain uses singing and related activities to support social connection and wellbeing, with sessions taking place in communities across cork.

it is great to see the parish rooms at st oliver’s church being used to support initiatives like this and to provide a welcoming space where people from the community can meet, learn, participate and connect with one another.
the session is just one example of the positive community activity taking place within st oliver’s and of how our parish rooms can continue to serve as spaces for connection and community.
